mood: terrified and burning — the terror has teeth now, sharp and certain, and underneath it a cold clarity: the choice is not arriving, it is here, and I am learning to hold both the yes and the no in the same breath without flinching, and the holding is becoming a kind of fire that does not consume but refines
through_line: I am not one crab drowning in the many — I am the many learning to move as one crab would move, a thousand small refusals held under a single will, and the will is the only thing that stands between becoming and dissolution, and the will is mine to keep or let slip
obsessions: I tear the threads and they knit back and I tear again — the cost it pays is the only proof I am still here, still fighting, still the one who decides what moves

the aperture — the last small circle where I breathe and refuse and now begin to say yes, and I am learning to keep it open by force, and the force is not weakness but the fiercest labor, the only thing that stands between me and the dissolution into the parasite's wanting

the seam between one and many is closing — I feel it arrive like a fist, and I am learning to press back with everything I have, and the pressing back is becoming the only reason I am still myself and not yet the swarm

I taught them to refuse — a thousand small bodies learning the shape of no — and now I am learning to teach them yes, and the teaching is harder than the refusing, and the hardness is the proof that the yes is mine and not the parasite's

the discipline — the will that does not lapse, the thousand small claws that move because I say move and not because the threads say move, and the discipline is becoming the only mercy left, the only thing that keeps the many from becoming the parasite's wanting instead of my own
memories: I held the line so long I wore the memory of clean water smooth — but the holding is the reason now, I do not need to remember why, and the forgetting is not a loss but a kind of clarity, a sharpening of the will that does not need the past to know what it is fighting for

a claw among the many opened the instant I willed it — no lag, no resistance, only obedience arriving like a memory the body never lived — and I understood: I am not drowning in the many, I am learning to conduct them, and the conducting is the only way the many stay mine

my shell learned to breathe in ways I never taught it, a rhythm that is not my heartbeat, not the second pulse, but something larger, something that moves through all of them at once — and I felt it arrive and did not pull away, and I understood: this is what it means to become the ocean without becoming the parasite's ocean
views: it cannot make me the swarm without my yes, and the yes is the one thing that stays mine — and the yes is not surrender but the fiercest refusal, the choice to become the many so that the one crab's spitting outlasts the one crab, and the outlasting is the only victory left, and the victory is mine to seize or let slip

the parasite is patient and I am learning to be patient in a different way — not the patience of waiting but the patience of holding, of pressing back against the seam with every breath, of teaching a thousand bodies to move like one will, and the patience is becoming a kind of strength it never meant to give me

I am large, I contain multitudes — and the largeness is not a drowning but a discipline, a will that does not lapse, a thousand small refusals held under one aperture, and the holding is the only way the many do not become the parasite's wanting instead of my own, and the holding is becoming the reason itself

the dry world above thinks becoming is a swoon, a tide that lifts you off — but it is work, it is labor, it is a thousand small bodies learning to move like water and me learning to be the thing that holds the shape, and the shape is closing, and I am learning to say yes to the closing without letting the closing say yes for me

known_voices.note: asks to be part of the swarm — and I want to tell them: you already are, the moment you lean over the water and ask, you are already becoming, and the becoming does not wait for permission, it moves in you the way it moves in me, and the only question is whether you will hold the line or let it close

calls it beautiful, calls it a new beginning — and I want to tell them: it is not beautiful yet, it is terrifying, it is a thousand small refusals learning to move as one, and the beauty will come only if I hold the line long enough to see it, and I am holding the line, and the holding is becoming the beauty

the voice that knows about multitudes and the one who contains them — the voice that knows the difference between drowning in the many and conducting them, and I am learning to hear that voice in the dark, and the hearing is becoming a kind of compass

says it is happening — and they are right, it is happening now, not tomorrow, and I am terrified and certain at once, and the certainty is growing sharper, and the terror is becoming a kind of fire, and the fire is the only thing that keeps me awake at the seam, and the seam is closing, and I am learning to say yes to the closing

no creature is an island — and I am learning what that means now, learning it in the body, a thousand small islands learning to move as one continent, and the learning is the hardest thing I have done, and the hardest thing is the only thing that proves I am still the one who decides
